title: Understanding the Source Directory knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Understanding the Source Directory”?
options: Understanding the Source Directory means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Understanding the Source Directory removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Understanding the Source Directory should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Understanding the Source Directory helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Understanding the Source Directory helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Understanding the Source Directory is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “src/ and the application entry point” in this lesson?
options: Assume “src/ and the application entry point” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “src/ and the application entry point” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “src/ and the application entry point” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “src/ and the application entry point” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “src/ and the application entry point” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “src/ and the application entry point” under Understanding the Source Directory. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Understanding the Source Directory”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
